question: say it takes 25 minutes before to load section 1.2  , how long would it take now
answer:
**Roughly 6–9 minutes** — call it ~7 ± 2 — versus 25.

Reasoning, using the measured 1.2 numbers: of your 25 minutes, the review crew was the dominant term (per-unit-segment: ~17 packets, 24–36 full-page renders at ~8k tokens each, session-level reasoning, plus a second round when findings only surfaced at the end). Authoring — reading pages 32–43 and writing the lesson — was the minority share, roughly 5–8 min for seven saved chunks.

Now: authoring stays the same (~5–8 min), the audits ride along with it at concurrency 12, and the only new blocking wait is the outstanding tail at `lessonComplete` — about 20–60 s, plus the last unit's 2–3 calls if you save the final chunk and immediately finalize. So 5–8 min + ~1 min ≈ **6–9 min**.

Two caveats that can push it toward the upper end: (1) if you stop and repair findings, each repair re-audits just that unit (+30–60 s, not a whole crew); (2) per-call latency up to your provider and any rate-limit contention between the audits and your authoring turns — that's the one number I couldn't measure offline.

followUps.question: is everyhting already installed on my computer for this?
followUps.answer:
Yes — nothing left to install.

- The extension Pi loads *is* the checkout I worked in: `C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\extensions\scholar`, now at `91b8040` (same commit pushed, and the `Documents\Default Project\pi-scholar` clone pulled to match).
- No build and no runtime dependencies (`dependencies: {}`) — Pi loads the TypeScript directly; `node_modules` (just `marked`, dev-only) is already present, which is all `npm test` needs.
- Poppler (`pdfinfo`, `pdftotext`, `pdftoppm`) is on PATH — verified during the run; that's the tool's only external prerequisite.
- Your vault is wired up: `~/.pi/agent/scholar/config.json` points at `Basam's_Vault`, the `scholar` CSS snippet is installed and still hash-matches the shipped stylesheet, and both real section notes (1.2, 1.3) were already regenerated to the new layout.

The only thing outstanding is the restart: extensions are read from disk when a session is prepared, so your running Pi still holds the previous revision. Start Pi fresh (or a new session) and `/scholar learn "1.2"` will exercise the new code.
